provenance.encoding: own JSON schema; principle/parameter names are the classical canon; descriptions and examples are self-authored in this repository; matrix cells verified cell-by-cell against the reference at build time (this script asserts shape, range and count)

principles.name: Segmentation
principles.description: Divide an object into independent parts; make it sectional; increase the degree of fragmentation (down to particles/fields).
examples: powdered metal instead of solid stock

principles.name: Taking out
principles.description: Extract the only-necessary part or property; move the required function into a separate object; separate the disturbing part out.
examples: pilot flame separate from the main burner
noise source relocated into an annex

principles.name: Local quality
principles.description: Make an object's parts homogeneous or locally adapted: each part conditions its function best; mismatch adjacent parts on purpose.
examples: graded-composition coating, hard at the wear face
per-forum gear ratios in one gearbox

principles.name: Asymmetry
principles.description: Change an object's symmetry; use asymmetry where symmetry is assumed; enhance an existing asymmetry.
examples: asymmetric fin spacing for bypass control
non-round piston profiles in wobble pumps

principles.name: Merging
principles.description: Bring identical or similar objects together; merge operations in time or space; make near-continuous processes simultaneous.

principles.name: Universality
principles.description: One object performs several functions; remove the need for others.
examples: the gantry that is also the conduit
a tool that measures and stirs

principles.name: Nesting
principles.description: Place one object inside another; nest objects by degree; make one part pass through a cavity in another.
examples: cabling routed inside the structural spar

principles.name: Anti-weight
principles.description: Counter-weight the mass with lift/levitation or an opposite force; aerodynamically or hydrodynamically shape it.

principles.name: Preliminary anti-action
principles.description: Pre-apply the counter-action; pre-stress or pre-tension against the known load; pre-set the opposite deformation.

principles.name: Preliminary action
principles.description: Do the required action (or part of it) in advance; pre-arrange objects so they engage from the right position.

principles.name: Beforehand cushioning
principles.description: Cushion in advance: compensate for low reliability with cheap emergency countermeasures prepared before harm occurs.
examples: burst discs upstream of relief trains

principles.name: Equipotentiality
principles.description: Change working conditions so lifting/positioning force is unneeded; operate in a field/equipotential frame; keep the potential gradient out of the process.

principles.name: The other way round
principles.description: Invert the action; make the fixed part move and the moving part fixed; turn the object upside-down or inside-out.
examples: rotating the die instead of the stock
immersion cooling instead of forced draft

principles.name: Spheroidality
principles.description: Move from straight lines/flat surfaces to curves, spheres, spirals; use rollers/balls/centrifugal forms.

principles.name: Dynamics
principles.description: Allow characteristics to change to be optimal at each stage; split into parts that move relative to each other.

principles.name: Partial or excessive actions
principles.description: If 100% is hard, do a little more or a little less: slight overshoot/back-off to reach the effect exactly.

principles.name: Another dimension
principles.description: Add a dimension; use multi-storey or tilted layouts; use another side of a surface.

principles.name: Mechanical vibration
principles.description: Cause periodic oscillation; change the frequency; use resonance or its absence; use phase instead of amplitude.

principles.name: Periodic action
principles.description: Replace continuous action with periodic action; change the period; use pulses/pauses between them.
examples: intermittent dosing instead of continuous feed

principles.name: Continuity of useful action
principles.description: Carry the useful action continuously; eliminate idle runs; combine operations in time.

principles.name: Rushing through
principles.description: Do harmful/fast actions at high speed — so fast the harm cannot propagate.

principles.name: Blessing in disguise
principles.description: Turn harm into benefit: use the harmful factor to deliver the effect; intensify it until it stops being harmful.

principles.name: Feedback
principles.description: Introduce feedback; amplify an existing feedback loop; invert it if it fights the goal.

principles.name: Intermediary
principles.description: Use an intermediary carrier or process; temporarily join one object to another for transport or transformation.

principles.name: Self-service
principles.description: Make the object serve itself: use waste energy/matter to perform the maintenance or auxiliary action.

principles.name: Copying
principles.description: Replace an expensive/fragile/dangerous object with cheap copies; use optical, acoustic or thermal images instead of the object.
examples: disposable wear coupons for corrosion monitoring

principles.name: Cheap short-living objects
principles.description: Replace an expensive durable object with a cheap short-lived one; sacrifice the cheap object repeatedly instead of maintaining the durable one.
examples: disposable filter cartridges vs cleaned media
consumable spray nozzles on slurry duty

principles.name: Mechanics substitution
principles.description: Replace a mechanical means with fields/optics/acoustics/thermal/chemical/electrical interaction.
examples: ultrasonic metering instead of a rotor

principles.name: Pneumatics and hydraulics
principles.description: Use gas/liquid pneumatic or hydraulic agents: cushions, hydraulics, foams, jets.

principles.name: Flexible shells and thin films
principles.description: Make interconnecting parts flexible or adaptive; move from fixed shells to flexible films/membranes.
examples: membrane gas transfer instead of sparging

principles.name: Porous materials
principles.description: Use porous/mesh materials; add pores by design; use capillary networks.

principles.name: Color changes
principles.description: Change an object's optical/color/finish properties; use additives that change transparency or emissivity.

principles.name: Homogeneity
principles.description: Make interacting objects of the same material (or near-compatible) so no third phase is introduced.
examples: like-on-like sliding pairs with hardness inversion
same-family gasket/pipe to stop galvanic attack

principles.name: Discarding and recovering
principles.description: After a function completes, discard the used part; restore it in-place during operation.

principles.name: Transformation of properties
principles.description: Change the physico-chemical state, density, conductivity, elasticity or temperature of the material or the field.

principles.name: Phase transitions
principles.description: Use phase transitions with volume/heat effects: expand, evaporate, freeze, sublime.

principles.name: Thermal expansion
principles.description: Exploit thermal expansion/contraction of materials; use bimetallic or mismatched-expansion assemblies.

principles.name: Strong oxidants
principles.description: Replace normal air with enriched oxygen; ionize it; use ozone; use aggressive chemistry in controlled dosage.

principles.name: Inert atmosphere
principles.description: Replace the normal environment or chemistry with an inert or neutral one; add inert additives or blankets.

principles.name: Composite materials
principles.description: Use composite/multi-material construction instead of homogeneous; combine materials at the grain or fiber scale.

parameters.name: Weight of moving object
parameters.description: Mass or gravitational load of a component that translates/rotates.

parameters.name: Weight of stationary object
parameters.description: Mass or load of a fixed component of the system.

parameters.name: Length of moving object
parameters.description: Principal linear dimension of a moving component.

parameters.name: Length of stationary object
parameters.description: Principal linear dimension of a fixed component.

parameters.name: Area of moving object
parameters.description: Surface area of a moving component (wear, drag, exchange faces).

parameters.name: Area of stationary object
parameters.description: Surface area of a fixed component (footprint, exchange faces).

parameters.name: Volume of moving object
parameters.description: Three-dimensional extent of a moving component.

parameters.name: Volume of stationary object
parameters.description: Three-dimensional extent of a fixed component.

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: Rate of the process or linear/rotational velocity of the object.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: Force or load the system exerts or must react against.

parameters.name: Stress or pressure
parameters.description: Internal stress or fluid pressure acting in the system.

parameters.name: Shape
parameters.description: External contours/geometry of the object.

parameters.name: Stability of composition
parameters.description: Compositional/structural stability of the object over time.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: Load-bearing capacity, ultimate or yield integrity of the object.

parameters.name: Duration of action by a moving object
parameters.description: Service life / duty duration of a moving component.

parameters.name: Duration of action by a stationary object
parameters.description: Service life / duty duration of a fixed component.

parameters.name: Temperature
parameters.description: Operating temperature level or its excursion range.

parameters.name: Illumination intensity
parameters.description: Light/optical intensity available to the process.

parameters.name: Energy use by a moving object
parameters.description: Energy consumed by the moving object to perform its function.

parameters.name: Energy use by a stationary object
parameters.description: Energy consumed by the stationary object (parasitic/holding).

parameters.name: Power
parameters.description: Rate of energy conversion (work per unit time).

parameters.name: Loss of energy
parameters.description: Energy lost to friction, leakage, radiation, conversion.

parameters.name: Loss of substance
parameters.description: Material lost to wear, evaporation, spillage, purge.

parameters.name: Loss of information
parameters.description: Data/signal lost in the process (sensing fidelity included).

parameters.name: Loss of time
parameters.description: Time lost to idle, sequencing, rework, changeover.

parameters.name: Amount of substance
parameters.description: Quantity of substance consumed, held, or produced per cycle.

parameters.name: Reliability
parameters.description: Probability the object performs its function when demanded.

parameters.name: Measurement accuracy
parameters.description: Closeness of a measurement to the true value.

parameters.name: Manufacturing precision
parameters.description: Achievable geometric/process precision of manufacture.

parameters.name: External harm affecting the object
parameters.description: Harmful influences arriving from the environment onto the object.

parameters.name: Object-generated harmful factors
parameters.description: Harmful emissions/fields the object itself generates.

parameters.name: Ease of manufacture
parameters.description: Ease (cost, steps) of fabricating the object.

parameters.name: Ease of operation
parameters.description: Ease (training, effort) of operating the object.

parameters.name: Ease of repair
parameters.description: Ease (time, access) of repairing the object.

parameters.name: Adaptability
parameters.description: Ability of the object to respond to changing conditions/uses.

parameters.name: Device complexity
parameters.description: Count and interrelation of the system's parts and controls.

parameters.name: Difficulty of detecting/measuring
parameters.description: Difficulty of inspecting, detecting or measuring the object.

parameters.name: Extent of automation
parameters.description: Degree to which the function runs without a human in the loop.

parameters.name: Productivity
parameters.description: Output quantity per unit time of the system.
